items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I would go and study with Dennis if I had nine days off with Nat, and everybody would go home, I'd go to Philadelphia and stay with Dennis.

ctx.x: Well, that inspires me, you know, and that actually makes me want to play. I sit and I listen and I listen and I listen, and I analyze what he's doing, and they -- technically he's great, and his ideas are great. And incidently he studied with a very dear friend of mine by the name of Dennis

Sandolee. Dennis Sandolee is a fair guitarist but a great mind. I mean he's a fair guitarist in that he doesn't confine himself to guitar. He teaches music to a saxophone player, pianists, whatever. I would go and study with Dennis if I had nine days off with Nat, and everybody would go home, I'd go to Philadelphia and stay with Dennis. And we just go through the whole thing.
So I could recognize-- when I heard Pat Martina I said, well he studied with Dennis Sandolee. I knew this. Coltrane studied with Dennis Sandolee. Yeah. He's a great mind.
